title: Proactive request resharding and tenant circuit repair runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a consolidated runbook and customer-escalation play for a class of incidents where regional request routing becomes uneven (request hotspots), tenant-level requests are effectively trapped on degraded regional backends, and KV cache desynchronization causes silent correctness regressions. The goal is a low-risk, observable sequence that:
- shifts new traffic away from degrading nodes/regions with tenant-priority awareness;
- reshards request allocation across serving partitions to avoid tenant starvation;
- performs a KV cache reconciliation gate to prevent stale prefix responses; and
- coordinates customer communication for Hosted and Dedicated customers without exposing internal topology.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to Hosted and Dedicated (multi-region) deployment modes. Private/VPC guidance included for customers with Redwood agent installed but assumes operator approval for network changes.
- Intended for incidents where latency and error-rate divergence between regions exceeds configured thresholds for >5 minutes and impacts >2% of tenant requests.
- Preserves tenant affinity where possible; preferred to avoid broad cold-cache flushes.

Detection triggers (automated):
- Per-tenant 1m error-rate > 5x baseline OR 95th latency > 1.5x SLO for three consecutive 1m windows.
- Cross-region replication lag metric (kv.repl.lag) > 10s AND prefix-miss-rate increase > 1%.
- Console alert: "region-request-imbalance" with >3 region nodes flagged.

Immediate mitigation (first 10 minutes):
1) Triage & communicate: open incident channel, run initial customer-impact query (per-route QPS and error breakdown). Notify customer success for any enterprise tenants flagged as "Dedicated" or "Private".
2) Apply per-tenant routing hold: increment tenant circuit weight to 0.25 for the affected region(s) using routing API (api.internal/routing/adjust). This is a soft throttle to allow graceful shedding.
3) Enable proxy-level request buffering threshold to 30s for affected region to avoid request storms to healthy regions.
4) Turn on verbose trace sampling for the tenant and request paths to capture KV cache keyspace hits/misses.

Resharding and traffic shaping sequence (safe path):
A) Snapshot current routing state and KV cache epoch for affected nodes (cmd: infractl snapshot-routing --region=A --out=...). Store snapshot link in incident timeline.
B) Create a temporary reshard map that moves 20-40% of the tenant's sticky shards to a healthy region (prefer lower-latency sibling regions). Apply with a canary: pick 5% of tenant traffic first and monitor 1m latency/error.
C) If canary stable for 3 consecutive 1m windows, progressively ramp to target over 10 minutes.
D) During ramp, keep KV reconciliation gate closed for moved shards: requests for moved prefixes route to owning region but are guarded by a cache-version check; if cache epoch mismatch, fall back to origin model variant that is stateless (small perf cost but correctness preserved).

KV reconciliation procedure (to run in parallel but gated):
1) Identify stale prefixes using kv.repl.diff tool and list of moved shard prefixes.
2) For prefixes with drift < 1000 keys, perform incremental apply (kv-sync --shards=...). For larger drifts, schedule background resync and keep served requests on fallback stateless variant until resync completes.
3) Verify post-sync by sampling 100 prefixes and asserting match-rate > 99.9%.

Rollback criteria and signals:
- Rollback immediately if error-rate for moved shards increases by >50% relative to pre-change baseline and does not stabilize within 2 minutes.
- Rollback if end-to-end latency for canary cohort rises above SLO by >2x.
- Rolling back: restore routing map from snapshot, reduce proxy buffer, and mark shards to be reconciled later via offline window.

Private/VPC operator notes:
- Because network and directory services are customer-controlled, coordinate with customer ops before applying any cross-region redirection. Use the operator-approved change channel and include customer consent stamp in the incident timeline.
- If operator disallows rerouting, prefer quota-throttling + explicit customer communication and a targeted maintenance window.

Customer communication template (for CS/SE use):
- Short: "We are actively mitigating a regional routing imbalance affecting some requests. We are shifting a small fraction of traffic to healthy regions and expect reduced errors within 15–30 minutes. We will update you at key milestones and share a post-incident summary."
- Postmortem bullet points to include: time window, tenant impact, actions taken, KV drift summary, recommended config changes.

Post-incident actions (owner assignments):
- Engineering: follow-up task to harden routing policy test coverage and add automated canary stability checks (ENG task).
- Observability: add dashboard panel for per-tenant kv.repl.diff and per-region thermal maps.
- Product/CS: contact impacted customers with runbook summary and remediation timeline.

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- We prefer gradual reshards to avoid cold-cache spikes; this increases complexity in KV reconciliation but lowers customer impact.
- We chose to use a stateless fallback variant to prioritize correctness over raw latency during reconciliation.

Artifacts and links:
- Draft routing API call examples: https://confluence.redwood/routing/reshard-examples
- Example PR for canary orchestration: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4231

Acceptance criteria for closing this ticket:
- Runbook validated in a simulated test with at least two tenants and one cross-region latency fault injected.
- Automated alert playbooks created (console alert + PagerDuty runbook) and ownership assigned.
- One tabletop run completed with SRE, Runtime, and CS teams.
